g.text: A linked slide show (ADR-0048 §8): Shift+S opens an audience window; either window drives; main numbers every move
slides-present-linked-fx: start the show from the
current slide WITHOUT fullscreen; presenter view on;
the sender is an app window's own webContents,
it is focused, it retains `path`, it is in no session →
claim a warm-pool window: mark it ephemeral (window.edn
is never written for it), un-maximize, place it on the other
display, showInactive() — window A keeps the focus
role: "audience", page: 2, blank: null, fullscreen: true}}
phase :live, known = the start (page 2); the interceptor runs once —
A has not moved, so nothing is sent; peer :waiting ("Waiting for the
audience window…"); a separate display and :slides-fullscreen? →
vv:set-fullscreen {on: true} for window A itself
:start {seq 0, page 2}; the deck opens in a tab
the deck mounts (:pdf/deck-detected) → the show starts at page 2
in the audience view; phase :live, known = the start (page 2, seq 0);
vv:set-fullscreen {on: true} for window B itself
the engine's first report {page 2, presenting? true} equals known →
nothing is sent: B never announces its page as a move (a move would be
ordered after any step A took while B loaded — and undo it)
peer :live — the pane's "Waiting…" notice goes away
the engine steps at once (renderer.pdf/step!) to page 3; its
report differs from known → move; out = {1}, known = page 3
{seq: 1, page: 3, blank: null} — to every other member
push seq 1 > 0, out = {} → known = page 3, and the EFFECT
no history entry; shown at once (a followed move
the engine's report {page 3} equals known → nothing is sent
(a window never echoes a move back)
both windows move at once — the moves cross
← clicked on the audience window (to page 2)
push seq 2 arrives while out = {1} → HOLD it: main ordered it
before B's own move, and showing it would take B back
ack 1 (seq 3): out = {} ; own-seq 3; the held seq 2 < 3 →
discard it: B's own move IS main's latest state
both windows show page 2 at seq 3 — main's last state — and nothing more is sent:
each window's report equals its known position. Proof and model check: docs/theory/11.
Escape in either window ends the show
slides-stop-fx → leave; B leaves the fullscreen it asked for
close() — the audience window existed only for the show
ended + stop → slides-stop-fx: the show ends; window A leaves
the fullscreen it asked for and returns to the view it had before
the presenter, the audience, their keys
a renderer window: re-frame, app.slides-link, the PDF engine
the IPC seam (preload, vv:presenter-* and vv:open-files)
main: the session model, the shell, the windows it opens
A move carries a whole position {page, blank}, never a step; `mid` is the sender's own counter.
